_meta.purpose: Canonical source of truth for the Orryx routine fleet schedule + dependency DAG. The live scheduler is ALIGNED to this file, not the reverse. Human-readable companion: ROUTINES.md.
_meta.revision_note: v2 2026-07-30 — WINDOW MOVE 04:32-10:34 -> 12:00-19:00 AEST. Root cause: the scheduler only dispatches while the desktop app is open, and the entire fleet block sat in hours the host is asleep (04:32-10:34 AEST = 18:32Z-00:34Z). On app-open the dispatcher replays missed slots in ascending slot order but caps at ~6 concurrent sessions; routines take 20-60 min each, so ~25 daily tasks needed 2+ hrs of continuous uptime to drain and never got it. The chronological tail (ceo -> daily-planner -> approval-gov -> execution-safety -> engineering -> r11 -> briefing-writer -> triage -> failure-analysis -> eod -> memory-consolidation) was never reached and read as 'dormant' on the beacon for 10 days. Fix is the window, NOT a dispatcher (a re-fire dispatcher was considered and rejected 2026-07-30 as fragile on the app-open-burst model). EVERY dependency gap in v2 is >= its v1 value - no ordering regression. Note: the scheduler adds a deterministic per-task jitter of up to ~9.5 min at dispatch, so actual fire times run a few minutes later than the cron value.
_meta.window: 12:00-19:00 AEST daily block; chosen because the host is reliably live in that range. Do NOT schedule fleet work outside it - anything before ~12:00 or after ~19:10 lands while the app is closed and only runs as a catch-up burst.
_meta.ordering_model: Wall-clock cron staggers by layer give correct order on a normal day; CORRECTNESS rests on the per-consumer producer pre-check (see _shared/PRODUCER_PRECHECK.md), NOT on the clock. A consumer whose same-day required input is absent SKIPs rather than consuming stale/older data.
_meta.cadence_rationale: Daily is justified only when the input changes daily AND a day of staleness causes harm. Freshness-critical (security, safety, repo state) + the operator-facing governance spine stay daily; strategic/evolution routines that synthesize slow-moving internal state run weekly/fortnightly or are condition-triggered with a NO_CHANGE skip.
_meta.circular_dep_adr: daily-planner <-> orchestration is broken by TEMPORAL SPLIT: orchestration runs terminal-of-day (N, 19:00) over the full same-day cohort and SEEDS the next day; daily-planner (N+1, 15:50) consumes the PRIOR-DAY master-operating-plan(N). The edge is one-directional across days: producers(N) -> orchestration(N) -> daily-planner(N+1), now a ~21h gap. Do NOT move orchestration earlier than the same-day cohort (would re-introduce the spine-gap race). v1 placed it at 23:30, which satisfied the ADR but sat outside every live-host window, so it went dark; 19:00 is the latest slot that is both after the full cohort and inside the window.

layers.L0: root producers — scan ground truth directly, never consume sibling reports
layers.L1: synthesis producers — consume L0, emit domain intelligence
layers.L2: specialised consumers — single-domain synthesis over L1
layers.L3: governance synthesizers — consume the full L2 cohort

failure-analysis-routine.note: UNCHANGED in v2 - already inside the window. Consumes PRIOR-DAY eod-summary, so it does not race same-day eod. MUST run before memory-consolidation.

orchestration-routine.note: TERMINAL synthesis - closes the window at 19:00, seeds next-day daily-planner (15:50). Moved from 23:30 in v2: 23:30 satisfied the ADR but sat outside every live-host window so it went dark. 19:00 is the latest slot that is both after the full same-day cohort and inside the window.

non_fleet_tasks._note: Live scheduled tasks not owned by the fleet DAG but moved into the window in v2 so they stop dying on the closed-app problem. Cadence for these is NOT otherwise stored durably - see the scheduler-registry-wipe memory.
non_fleet_tasks._produces_note: produces added 2026-07-31 so fleet-health can dormancy-check these (was FH-45). Each path is taken from the task's own SKILL.md, not its description. produces_verified=true means an artifact matching the template was found on disk; false means the routine is CONTRACTED to write it but has never been observed doing so - treat a miss as 'unproven path OR dormant', not as confirmed dormancy, until the first artifact appears. produces=null means the task emits to the session only by design and CANNOT be dormancy-checked by file existence; do not invent a path for these. {isoweek} = ISO year-week, e.g. 2026-W31.
